title: Redistribute Characters to Make All Strings Equal
statement:
You have a list of strings `words`. A move takes one character out of some non-empty string `words[i]` and inserts it anywhere inside a different string `words[j]` (`i != j`). You may make as many moves as you like, including none.

Return `true` if some sequence of moves can leave all the strings in `words` identical to each other, and `false` if that can never happen.
constraints: words[i] contains only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

A move only relocates a character; it never creates, deletes or changes one, and it can drop the character at any position. So the order of letters inside a string is irrelevant, and the only question is whether the total supply of each letter can be shared out equally. If there are `n` strings and the letter `x` appears `c` times overall, every final string must contain exactly `c / n` copies of `x`, which needs `c` to be a multiple of `n`. When that holds for every letter, moving characters around can always build the same word in each slot.

## Approach

1. Make an array `counts` of 26 zeros, one per letter.
2. Walk every character of every word and add one to its letter's count.
3. For each `count`, if it is not divisible by `words.length`, return `false`.
4. Otherwise every letter splits evenly, so return `true`.

## Example 1, step by step

`words = ["abc", "aabc", "bc"]`, so there are 3 strings. Counting all characters gives `a: 3`, `b: 3`, `c: 3`, and every other letter 0. Each of these is a multiple of 3, so no check fails and the answer is `true`: each string ends up as some arrangement of `a`, `b`, `c`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(L), where L is the total number of characters, since each is counted once and the final loop has 26 steps.
- Space: O(1): the count array always has 26 slots.

## Pitfalls

- Only divisibility matters; the original lengths of the strings do not, because characters can move freely.
- Letters with a count of 0 pass the check automatically, so they need no special case.
- A single word is always fine: every count is divisible by 1.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `counts` | how many times each letter appears across all words |
| `word`, `ch` | the word and character currently being counted |
| `count` | one letter's total, tested for divisibility by `words.length` |

narration.2: Prepare one counter for each of the 26 lowercase letters.
narration.3: Visit every word in the list.
narration.4: Visit every character inside that word.
narration.5: Add one to the counter of this character's letter.
narration.8: Look at the total for each letter.
narration.9: A letter whose total cannot be split evenly among all the words blocks equal strings.
narration.10: So the answer is false as soon as such a letter appears.
narration.13: Every letter divides evenly, so the words can all be made identical.
